description: The mirror contract. This repository is one half of a mirror; the other is packages/agent-sdk/agent-sdk-js in stiggio/stigg-sdk, where the SDK is developed. A mirrored file has the same path on both sides modulo one directory prefix - here the prefix is empty, because the package is the repository - which is what keeps a sync a reviewable diff rather than a translation. Read by the sync agent, enforced by tools/repo-tests.

notes.prefix: packages/agent-sdk/agent-sdk-js/** on the internal side, ** here.
sync: Read this pair's lastSyncedCommit for the source side from .sync-state.json.
git diff <lastSyncedCommit>..HEAD -- <source path> is the whole change set.
Apply it under the destination prefix, then apply the transforms below.
Run: yarn lint && yarn typecheck && yarn test && yarn build.
Update .sync-state.json for both sides in the same pull request.
Every commit carries the trailer Stigg-Sync-Source: <repo>@<sha>.
neverInASync: A change to a path listed in internalOnly or repositoryOnly.
A workspace: range in the manifest, or a paths block in the tsconfig.
A tracked path no rule here accounts for - the guard fails so the decision gets made.
Formatting-only churn: it means the formatter configurations have drifted. Fix that first.
notes.dependencyUpdates: They happen internally, where the SDK is developed, and arrive by sync. Nothing here proposes bumps of its own: two bots editing one mirrored manifest from opposite ends is a conflict with a schedule attached.
notes.secrets: .env and examples/demo.env are gitignored on both sides, so a sync that copies tracked files cannot carry one. tools/repo-tests/no-secrets.test.ts is the guard for the day one is committed anyway.
notes.layout: The package is the repository root (openSource.path "."), because one duck-typed package serves every vendor - the recipes under src/bindings carry no vendor dependency, so there is nothing a package-per-adapter split would separate. If that ever changes, the move is: git mv the mirrored paths under packages/<name>/, set openSource.path to it, and split package.json into a workspace root and the package. The guards read this field rather than assuming a layout, so they do not change with it.
notes.changelog: CHANGELOG.md is this repository's own: the internal monorepo generates none (nx release has projectChangelogs and workspaceChangelog both false), and nothing is published from here. Each sync appends what arrived and the upstream commit it came from.

package-json.description: One manifest is both the package and the repository here, so this is a merge: mirrored keys cross, and the keys listed under `openSourceOnly` are this repository's own tooling and never travel. Nothing is published from this side, so the publishing fields are not mirrored at all.

fields.why: The monorepo builds it from source; here it is an ordinary published dependency.
The package is the repository root here, so there is no subdirectory to name.

fields.internal: rm -rf dist && yarn run -T tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit && yarn run -T tsc -p tsconfig.build.json
fields.openSource: rimraf dist && tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.build.json
fields.why: `yarn run -T` is the monorepo's top-level runner; there is no workspace above this one.
The repository guards run alongside the package's own suite here.

package-json.why: `private: true` and the absence of `files`/`publishConfig` are deliberate: nothing is released from this repository, and `@stigg/agent-sdk-js` on npm keeps coming from the monorepo. `main` and `typings` point at `src` on both sides, so they are not transformed.

tsconfig.description: The open-source file is the internal `tsconfig.json` merged with the `tsconfig.base.json` it extends: same effective options, nothing left to extend.

fields.why: Inlined. A change to the internal base has to be re-merged into this file by hand - there is no other link between them.

fields.internal: <7 entries pointing at sibling packages' dist/*.d.ts>
fields.why: Dependencies are ordinary node_modules here; there is nothing to redirect.
`tools/` is this repository's own, and is linted and type-checked with everything else.

readme.description: The package README is this repository's front page. The prose is mirrored; what differs is how a reader is told to run things, because there is no workspace to address.

fields.why: Mechanical, and bounded to these script names so the rewrite is reversible.

fields.internal: Says the examples live beside the source in the Stigg SDK monorepo, with paths relative to it.
fields.openSource: Says the examples live in this repository, with paths relative to its root.
fields.why: Maintained by hand on each side; a sync reviews it rather than rewriting it.

fields.internal: Describes resolving workspace siblings through `paths`, built first by Nx.
fields.why: Same: two sentences that are true on one side only.

fields.openSource: The framing this repository adds: that it is a mirror, that it publishes nothing, and the licence.
fields.why: A repository front page needs them; a package README inside a monorepo does not.
